### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e287974e2d2fcff54b67a89d14bbb6bba9c3ead` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d57234f169695cc996a1dd660367fbedc9df9466` — the merge of head `080522f71ac8269dd9a4e4893f148e85bd0269fa` into base `6e287974e2d2fcff54b67a89d14bbb6bba9c3ead`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d57234f169695cc996a1dd660367fbedc9df9466 && git checkout d57234f169695cc996a1dd660367fbedc9df9466
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6e287974e2d2fcff54b67a89d14bbb6bba9c3ead 080522f71ac8269dd9a4e4893f148e85bd0269fa && git checkout -B drift-repro 6e287974e2d2fcff54b67a89d14bbb6bba9c3ead && git merge --no-ff 080522f71ac8269dd9a4e4893f148e85bd0269fa

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e287974e2d2fcff54b67a89d14bbb6bba9c3ead
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

Request: review · area A5 · head 080522f71a

Fixes #33487. The durable http node resolves its verb once (`cfg.method ?? (durable ? 'POST' : 'GET')`) and both the outbox enqueue and the no-outbox fallback (`sendInline`, awaited and save-path background) use it. On main the fallback sent GET: with a body, fetch refused it and nothing was sent; without a body, a bodyless GET counted as acted 0. Pins: 5 cases on the real-receiver harness (same POST, bytes and signature as the outbox; control: a request/response node with no method still GETs). Ablation 4 red, control green. Clause-② no, Metadata-protocol none, +122/-4 in service-automation. Head 080522f71a is 2393fb35 plus a clean merge of origin/main to pick up #33543 (Test Core 8/8 at 2393fb35 was the plugin-approvals action-page-member timeout). os-dev report: 6888299149.

Posted 2026-11-15T03:09Z.

## Review: PASS

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A5 · Fixes #33487 (p2) · head `080522f71ac8269dd9a4e4893f148e85bd0269fa` · Clause-② no. CI on this head: 51 check runs, 35 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed. Test Core is 8/8 shards green, so the #33508 approvals flake did not fire.

**What was checked**

- **Scope.** The head is `2393fb35` plus a merge of main (`6e287974`). `git diff 6e287974..080522f7` is exactly the PR's 3 files, +122/-4, the same as `git diff 4bba8b8f..2393fb35` against the merge base. So the merge brought nothing else in, and only service-automation changes (`http-nodes.ts`, `http-node-signing.test.ts`, one changeset).
- **One verb on every send path.** On the merge base, the enqueue used `cfg.method ?? 'POST'` (l.379) and `sendInline` used `cfg.method ?? 'GET'` (l.284). Now `const method = cfg.method ?? (durable ? 'POST' : 'GET')` is resolved once, after the parse, and read by:
  - the outbox enqueue;
  - `sendInline`, which serves the awaited no-outbox fallback, the save-path background `void sendInline()`, and the plain request/response arm.

  Retries and redelivery cannot drift. The verb is stored on the `sys_http_delivery` row at enqueue (`memory-http-outbox.ts:81` and `sql-http-outbox.ts:192`), read back at `sql-http-outbox.ts:646`, and sent by `http-sender.ts` `sendOnce` (`delivery.method ?? 'POST'`). On the enqueue arm `durable` is always true, so the value enqueued is the same as on main. A flow-level retry runs the node again and resolves the same value.
- **An explicit `cfg.method` still wins** on every arm, because `??` checks it first. **A non-durable node is unchanged**: it resolves `cfg.method ?? 'GET'`, the same as before.
- **Verb, body, headers and signature agree.** In `sendInline`, the read/act accounting (`reads = /^(GET|HEAD|OPTIONS)$/i`), the `fetch` method, the bytes sent (`requestBody`) and the HMAC over those bytes all come from the same `method` and `requestBody`. An accepted fallback POST therefore counts `acted: 1`, and a rejected one counts `unmeasuredEffect`. Both follow the existing #4354 rule.
- **The behaviour change is a fix, not a changed answer.** Three sources already said POST when durable:
  - `HttpConfigSchema.method` ("default GET; POST when durable"; its jsdoc explains why there is no static `.default()`);
  - the descriptor ("GET by default; POST when the request is delivered in the background");
  - the outbox arm.

  Only the no-outbox fallback differed. With a body, that GET was never sent, because `fetch` refuses a GET with a body (os-dev report; I did not re-run it). Without a body, it sent a bodyless GET that claimed `acted: 0`, which is a false "changed nothing". No one could rely on the first. The second was the degraded arm of a durable callout, which contradicted the declared default. The changeset declares the change and gives the opt-out (`method: 'GET'`).
- **Tests.** I read the new `describe` in the real-receiver harness. The outbox arm is driven end to end through `HttpDispatcher.tick()` and used as the reference. Against it:
  - the awaited fallback (no messaging, and messaging without an outbox) and the `afterUpdate` background fallback match the reference on verb, received body bytes and signature header, and the signature verifies;
  - the bodyless fallback POSTs and counts `acted: 1`;
  - the CONTROL request/response node with no method still GETs, signed over the empty body, `acted: 0`.

  The `vi` import is used (`vi.waitFor`). Per the os-dev report (comment 6888299149 on #33487), putting back `cfg.method ?? 'GET'` in `sendInline` turns 4 of 33 red and leaves the CONTROL green. I did not re-run that.

**Semver**

`patch` for `@objectstack/service-automation` holds.
- Metadata-protocol: none. No `packages/spec` file changed. The declared default ("POST when durable") is unchanged, and the runtime now applies it on the one arm that did not.
- Clause-②: no. No root export, accepted input or served shape is added.
- This is not a changed default that an author's metadata relies on: the default the metadata declares is the one now sent.

**Nits (none blocking)**

- **N1.** The `HttpConfigSchema.method` jsdoc (`packages/spec/src/automation/io-node-config.zod.ts`, ~l.1097–1099) still quotes the old spellings: "`method: cfg.method ?? 'POST'` on the durable arm, `const method = cfg.method ?? 'GET'` on the inline one". Its meaning is still true, but the quoted code no longer exists. The author already noted this as out of scope. It is worth fixing in a later spec-touching change.
- **N2.** The changeset says both paths send "the same body and signature the outbox would deliver". That holds for the object body the tests pin. It does not hold everywhere:
  - For a bodyless node, the outbox sends `'{}'` (`payload: body ?? {}` → `deliveryBody`) and signs it, while the fallback sends no body and signs `''`.
  - For a string body, the outbox sends the string verbatim, while the fallback JSON-encodes it.
  - The fallback also sends no `Content-Type: application/json`, which `sendOnce` sets.

  All of this predates the PR, and the author lists the byte differences as out of scope. Only the release-note wording overclaims.
- **N3.** No test pins an explicit `method` on the durable no-outbox fallback, for example `durable: true, method: 'GET'` or `'PUT'` with no outbox. The changeset gives `method: 'GET'` as the opt-out, so a one-case pin would cover it. The code makes it plain that the explicit method wins.

This is the final round from review#2 unless the head changes.
